open_points.subject: 01_models.md:preamble
open_points.text:
Field types and the complete field lists belong to the
State 6 model closure.
open_points.question: Replace this deferral with complete field lists in which every field has a type.

open_points.subject: 01_models.md:Model M01 — ObjectConnection
open_points.text:
The owner
creates and confirms it; the deliverer only reads it.
open_points.question: Who mints the ObjectConnection entity: the owner when creating the connection record, or the Registry when issuing project_id?
options: The owner mints the ObjectConnection, using a Registry-minted project_id
The Registry mints the ObjectConnection itself
The deliverer mints it from an owner command and a Registry-minted project_id
open_points.default_guess: The owner mints the ObjectConnection record, while the Registry mints only its project_id.

witness.initial: The Registry has issued project_id P, but no ObjectConnection exists.
events: The owner connects project P to its folders.
outcomes: The owner creates and therefore mints the ObjectConnection; the Registry minted only P.
The ObjectConnection is treated as already minted by the Registry because P exists, and the owner merely supplies folder facts.
witness.observer: The owner and any component enforcing creation authority or audit provenance.

open_points.subject: 01_models.md:Model M01 — ObjectConnection
open_points.question: What is the source of truth for an ObjectConnection while it is unconfirmed?
options: The same owner-created record is authoritative in both statuses
An unconfirmed draft has a different source of truth
No ObjectConnection exists until confirmation
open_points.default_guess: The owner-created record is the source of truth before and after confirmation.

open_points.subject: 01_models.md:Model M01 — ObjectConnection
open_points.question: Is this the final lifecycle, and can a confirmed connection ever be unconfirmed, replaced, disabled, or otherwise changed?
options: Final one-way lifecycle: unconfirmed to confirmed only
Confirmation can be revoked on the same entity
Changing folders creates or replaces a connection rather than changing the existing entity
open_points.default_guess: Use a final one-way unconfirmed-to-confirmed lifecycle; folder edits retain the same confirmed entity.

open_points.subject: 01_models.md:Model M01 — ObjectConnection
open_points.text: The same object stays connected while its folders or its confirmation change.
open_points.question: Which product action and actor may change the folders, label, or confirmation of the continuing ObjectConnection?
options: The owner updates all mutable connection facts
The Registry updates some facts and the owner controls confirmation
Folder or label changes require a replacement connection
open_points.default_guess: An owner connection-management action updates the label, folders, and confirmation on the same entity.

open_points.subject: 01_models.md:Model M01 — ObjectConnection
open_points.question: Is ObjectConnection required to be durably persisted, or may it be reconstructed or held transiently?
options: Durably persisted by the deliverer
Read from an external owner or Registry record on demand
Transient runtime configuration
open_points.default_guess: Durably persist it in the deliverer's backend.

open_points.subject: 01_models.md:Model M02 — SourcePhotoObservation
open_points.question: What fact does `duplicate` assert, including whether duplication is within one folder, one project, or all projects?
options: Another file in the same project has the same source content
A placement for the same project and source content already exists
The same content exists anywhere across projects
open_points.default_guess: It means another observed file in the same project has the same source content; an existing placement is represented by `placed` or `published`.

open_points.subject: 01_models.md:Model M03 — PreparedPhoto
open_points.text: Two prepared images with equal bytes and equal moments serve the same placement.
open_points.question: Does `how that moment was obtained` participate in PreparedPhoto value identity, or are values with different `exif`/`file_modified` provenance equal?
options: Provenance participates in equality with bytes and moment
Only bytes and moment determine equality
Provenance is not part of PreparedPhoto and belongs to the placement record only
open_points.default_guess: Include provenance in PreparedPhoto value identity because it is stated as one of the model's facts.

witness.initial: Two source files prepare to identical pixels and the same UTC moment; one moment came from EXIF and the other from file modification time.
events: The deliverer constructs a PreparedPhoto for each source.
outcomes: The two PreparedPhoto values are equal because their bytes and moments are equal.
The two PreparedPhoto values differ because their `exif` and `file_modified` provenance differs.
witness.observer: The placement logic and any equality, caching, or test code handling PreparedPhoto.

open_points.subject: 01_models.md:Model M04 — PhotoPlacement
open_points.text:
the `file_ref`, the hash, size and
media type of the stored image
open_points.question: Is `the hash` the SHA-256 source_id of the original content, a hash of the prepared stored image, or an additional field containing one of each?
options: The source-content SHA-256, identical to source_id
A hash of the prepared stored image
Both source-content and stored-image hashes
open_points.default_guess: Store both concepts explicitly: source_id for the original content and a separate hash for the prepared stored image.

witness.initial: A source JPEG is rotated and stripped of metadata during preparation, so its bytes differ from the stored image.
events: The deliverer hashes the source content to obtain source_id.
The deliverer prepares and stores the transformed image.
outcomes: The placement's `hash` equals source_id and identifies the original bytes.
The placement's `hash` identifies the transformed bytes in the binary store.
witness.observer: A caller or integrity checker comparing the placement record with either the source file or stored binary.

open_points.subject: 01_models.md:Model M04 — PhotoPlacement
open_points.question: Is `placed` definitively the only terminal status of PhotoPlacement, including after publication or loss of the stored binary?
options: Final lifecycle consists only of terminal `placed`
Publication changes the placement's status
Missing or invalid stored data changes or invalidates the placement
open_points.default_guess: Keep PhotoPlacement permanently terminal as `placed`; publication is represented only by PublicationMark.

open_points.subject: 01_models.md:Model M04 — PhotoPlacement
open_points.question: Is durable persistence of every PhotoPlacement required?
options: Every successful placement is durably persisted
A placement may be reconstructed from the binary store
Only publication marks are durable
open_points.default_guess: Require durable persistence for every successful placement.

open_points.subject: 01_models.md:Model M05 — PhotoPublication
open_points.question: From what fact is `intake_id` minted, by whom, and is it stable for every replay of the same placement?
options: The deliverer deterministically derives it from the placement identity
The deliverer generates and persists a new identifier when M04 is created
The calling flow supplies it
The Portal supplies it
open_points.default_guess: The deliverer deterministically derives a stable intake_id from project_id and source_id when creating M04.

witness.initial: A placement exists and its publication call must be retried after the first response is lost.
events: The deliverer builds the first PhotoPublication body.
The calling flow retries and obtains or rebuilds the body.
outcomes: The retry carries the same intake_id and the Portal treats it as the same publication.
The retry carries a newly minted intake_id and the Portal can treat it as another publication.
witness.observer: The calling flow and the Client Portal.

open_points.subject: 01_models.md:Model M05 — PhotoPublication
open_points.question: What model fact supplies `intake_source`, and what value does the first version put in it?
options: A fixed Portal Deliverer source value
A value derived from the calling flow
A value derived from the source folder or device
A value supplied by the owner
open_points.default_guess: Use a fixed value identifying Portal Deliverer.

open_points.subject: 01_models.md:Model M06 — PlacementOutcome
open_points.text:
`placed`, `replayed` or `failed`, the
reason of a failure, the placement facts when there is a placement, and the Portal `photo_id`
when the photo is already marked as published.
open_points.question: For an already published source, is the outcome status `replayed`, and must it contain both the placement facts and photo_id, or is publication a distinct outcome not represented by the listed statuses?
options: `replayed` with placement facts and photo_id
`placed` with placement facts and photo_id
A distinct `published` outcome status is missing
open_points.default_guess: Return `replayed` with the original placement facts and the recorded photo_id.

open_points.subject: 01_models.md:Model M07 — PublicationMark
open_points.text:
The calling flow creates it right after
`photo.publish` answers.
open_points.question: Does the calling flow mint and submit a complete PublicationMark, or does it request that the deliverer mint the mark from placement identity and photo_id?
options: The calling flow mints the complete mark
The deliverer mints it from a record-publication command
The calling flow supplies facts while the deliverer alone mints marked_at and commits the entity
open_points.default_guess: The calling flow submits project_id, source_id, and photo_id; the deliverer mints and durably commits the PublicationMark.

open_points.subject: 01_models.md:Model M07 — PublicationMark
open_points.text:
It carries the `project_id`, the
`source_id`, the Portal `photo_id` and `marked_at`.
open_points.question: Who supplies `marked_at`, and which event does it timestamp?
options: The deliverer's successful durable write time
The calling flow's time immediately after Portal publication
A publication timestamp returned by the Portal
open_points.default_guess: The deliverer supplies marked_at as the time the mark is first durably written.

witness.initial: The calling-flow clock and deliverer clock differ, and the Portal response contains its own publication time.
events: The calling flow publishes the photo.
The calling flow records the publication at the deliverer.
outcomes: marked_at records the caller's post-publication time.
marked_at records the deliverer's first-write time.
witness.observer: The owner or an audit/reporting flow reading the mark.

open_points.subject: 01_models.md:Model M07 — PublicationMark
open_points.text: The same `photo_id` again returns the first mark; another `photo_id` is refused.
open_points.question: Are these rules scoped to repeated marking of the same placement, or is a Portal photo_id globally unique across all PublicationMarks?
options: The rule is scoped to one placement; another placement may carry the same photo_id
photo_id is globally unique and may belong to only one PublicationMark
Reusing a photo_id for another placement returns the first placement's mark
open_points.default_guess: Require photo_id to be globally unique, while idempotent return and conflicting-photo refusal are evaluated for the same placement.

witness.initial: Placement A is marked with Portal photo_id X; placement B has no mark.
events: The calling flow attempts to mark placement B with the same photo_id X.
outcomes: A new mark for B is accepted because the idempotency rule is scoped independently to each placement.
The request is refused because X already belongs to A and photo_id is globally unique.
witness.observer: The calling flow recording publication for placement B.

open_points.subject: 01_models.md:Model M07 — PublicationMark
open_points.question: Is `marked` definitively permanent and terminal even if the Portal photo later becomes unavailable or deletion is introduced?
options: The mark is permanently terminal and never changes
The mark can be invalidated or retired
A removed Portal photo causes deletion of the mark
open_points.default_guess: For the current product, keep `marked` permanent and terminal; any future Portal deletion requires a new owner decision.

open_points.subject: 01_models.md:Model M07 — PublicationMark
open_points.question: Is durable persistence of PublicationMark required for the no-republication guarantee?
options: Every mark must be durably persisted before success is returned
A mark may be reconstructed from the Portal
A mark may be transient and retained only during the flow
open_points.default_guess: Require durable persistence before the record-publication action succeeds.
